answer: Before dawn on a fixed day, a claimant fells, mills, and stacks one marked cord of timber at a named riverside mill, branding each log with a falcon stamp burned into the grain. Two forest wardens count the stacked cords at sunrise, match each brand to the registry, and check the saw marks against the claimant's registered saw. A copied brand or mismatched saw voids the claim, burns a 180-credit stake, and bars the claimant's mill two seasons. A thousand counterfeits need a thousand cords cut, branded, and stacked by hand in one night, while one honest miller finishes one cord by breakfast.
